variants.architecture: forward-heavy stepped shoulder / tapering aft spine
variants.direction: The main mass is in broad HIGH FORWARD SHOULDERS immediately behind the unchanged cabin. Each shoulder is an angular wedge, flared sideways, with an oblique decorated face and a deep lower undercut. From this strong front mass the roof steps DOWN twice toward a narrow lower aft spine; in top view the body tapers conspicuously toward the stern. Its side profile must NOT have a horizontal constant-depth bar. Two unequal independent engines are vertically stacked on a short, exposed solid stern seat. A small raked fixed tail shield terminates the spine without bridging on posts. Three broad clipped trapezoidal wing leaves per side pivot beneath the FRONT shoulder and fan down/out/back. Adapt the relief into separate triangular shoulder fans, short tapering flute bands and a small aft panel; no long rectangular picture frame. Preserve enough side clearance under the shoulders for folded leaves. Primary gesture: monumental front shoulders flowing into a lighter dropping tail.
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE complete new pirate Liberty elite FIGHTER concept sheet for Freelancer. Design a purposeful assembly of sculpted planar masses with changing width and height, substantial joints and meaningful cutbacks. References:
1. EXACT IMMUTABLE current cockpit. Copy its low elongated capsule shell, thin existing frames, large blue-grey side glazing, long central roof pane, small rear panes and rounded glazed nose; preserve its size and proportions. 3. WING MOTION PRINCIPLE ONLY: three independent broad overlapping leaves on EACH side, compact sequential pivot chain near the forward root, spreading outward/back in flight and nesting backward along the hull when stowed. Each leaf stays full size. New solid root brackets and leaf outlines can change; leave clearance for the folded package. No rods or skeletal frames.
4. Historic Liberty sketches, inspiration for varied planar massing and engineered relationships, not their different cockpit or large circular fuselages.

Small cargo hatch: two flush longitudinal doors on a local roof patch, FORE-AFT center seam, modest outward/upward opening clearance. variants.visual_review: Читаются высокие передние плечи, ступенчатое понижение к узкой корме и отдельная вертикальная пара двигателей. Рельеф распределён по наклонным плечам и листам, длинный прямоугольный борт исчез. Три листа показаны раскрытыми и сложенными; реальный зазор пакета не проверен. Кабина сохраняет исходный тип, её точный контур берётся из CMP. Люк компактен, мелкое деление на TOP неоднозначно.

variants.architecture: Y plan with solid diverging aft prongs / lateral engines
variants.direction: Make a clear Y-shaped hull in TOP view. A short central forebody behind the native cockpit divides into TWO thick angular aft prongs, diverging gently around a substantial open central stern notch. Each prong ends in a separate rear-facing engine; the engines are a LEFT/RIGHT pair in this proposed layout. The prongs are tapered load-bearing shell volumes, not thin booms or skeletal frames. A short fixed transverse structural saddle joins them at the fork's base, well FORWARD of the open stern notch. Each outer flank carries a three-leaf swept wing fan from a compact FRONT root, with its stowed package outboard of the prong and clear of exhaust. Use wider prow shoulders and descending prong tops. A small paired hatch lies on the central forebody before the fork. Each prong has its own slanted shallow palmette relief; an axial stepped motif ties the fork into one authored shape. No centerline rectangular bar extending to the stern. This is a compact split-tail fighter, not a catamaran capital ship.

variants.visual_review: Явная Y-компоновка, глубокая выемка между массивными кормовыми ветвями, два боковых двигателя. Орнамент адаптирован к отдельным наклонным объёмам. Пакет крыльев расположен снаружи ветвей; его реальный проход требует моделирования. Кабина узнаваема, но её геометрия остаётся исходной, а не скопированной из арта.

variants.architecture: descending belly / narrow upper bridge / vertical engines low
variants.direction: Develop a deep ANGULAR VENTRAL KEEL below the longitudinal cockpit axis. The native cabin joins a short narrow upper deck; the main hull descends diagonally into a broad lower wedge toward the middle and aft. The upper rear deck cuts back strongly so the low rear engine assembly is visible above and behind the keel. Two unequal engines sit VERTICALLY STACKED on a compact rear seat low on the wedge. The silhouette has a strong diagonal descent and an under-slung mass, not a box at canopy height. Keep total height within about 1.2 times the source fighter height. Full three-leaf wing fans mount to substantial forward lower cheek sockets and spread on either side of the keel; when folded they run outside its side faces. A small hatch occupies the short top deck just behind the cabin. Ornament uses a triangular descending fan relief across each keel face, a quiet upper ledge and short fluted end fields. No tall freestanding dorsal tower or high car spoiler.

variants.architecture: deliberate balanced asymmetry / staggered lateral engines
variants.direction: Explore ONE deliberately ASYMMETRIC pirate reconstruction around the unchanged CENTERED native cockpit. Keep a short compact angular central core with full depth. The PORT side has a taller, longer solid armored engine cheek with a clipped trapezoidal top; the STARBOARD side has a lower shorter exposed engine seat and a deeply cut-back shoulder. Both rear-facing engines form an offset left/right pair, at slightly different fore-aft positions; both are visibly and solidly attached, never a loose jumble. The body should visibly differ from left to right in TOP but remain believable and balanced. Preserve three moving fan leaves PER SIDE with their compact forward roots and broadly similar flight span; brackets compensate for the unequal shoulders. Ornament survives as a fine stepped palmette field on the intact taller cheek, while the lower replaced side has a simpler broad angular fan and plain repair metal. Make the asymmetric volumes visible, not just different colors. Small centered roof hatch. No huge single off-center pod, no extra cabin, no round bulges. One of ten exploratory schemes, still clearly Liberty.

It is the forward tip, with no added beak. No changes to cabin or canopy. The neck and collar BEHIND it may be completely redesigned.
2. STYLE SAMPLE ONLY: look at the bottom-right DETAIL crop, its shallow sculpted Empire frieze, fan motifs, fine fluting, angular palmettes, stepped surrounds and medium-scale relief depth. Its long rectangular ship architecture is REJECTED. Do not copy that architecture, wings or engine housings. Redistribute similar craftsmanship to the new structure's differently shaped surfaces.
3. WING MOTION PRINCIPLE ONLY: three independent broad overlapping leaves on EACH side, compact sequential pivot chain near the forward root, spreading outward/back in flight and nesting backward along the hull when stowed. Each leaf stays full size. New solid root brackets and leaf outlines can change; leave clearance for the folded package. No rods or skeletal frames.
4. Historic Liberty sketches, inspiration for varied planar massing and engineered relationships, not their different cockpit or large circular fuselages.

Small cargo hatch: two flush longitudinal doors on a local roof patch, FORE-AFT center seam, modest outward/upward opening clearance. Combined length roughly one quarter of the main body's length; a secondary feature. Ornament respects each moving part and hatch boundary. Mechanical parts remain readable, but no gratuitous pipes, greeble carpet, rivet arrays, floating pieces or thin rod cages.
Empire aesthetic: authored shallow sculptural compositions adapted to angled facets, broad bands, shoulder fields, keel and wing leaves. Rays, palmettes, low medallions and recessed stepped borders. Relief casts real shadows, not only painted gold lines. Keep breathing space and native-scale surfaces. No freestanding statues, cathedral towers, crowns or ornate furniture. This is an agile FIGHTER with the native cabin, not a capital ship. Pirate service appears as a few deliberate plain repair insets and replaced skin sections. Muted native oxidized copper/rust, warm metal relief edges, dark recesses, original blue-grey glazing; material wear must not bury the design.

Presentation: pale warm-grey studio sheet, refined industrial concept illustration, crisp form shading with raking light. ONE large side-biased three-quarter view (nose LEFT, see top and side with minimal foreshortening), plus small SIDE, TOP (nose UP), REAR and STOWED views of the SAME design. Large view occupies most of the page. Keep all massing, engines, cabin and wing count consistent. STOWED shows the same whole leaves rotated backward, not miniaturized. For vertically stacked engines, TOP has one centered overlapping projection, never a false left/right pair. Labels only concept code and SIDE / TOP / REAR / STOWED. Compose as a landscape sheet.

ARCHITECTURE, HIGHEST PRIORITY:
Explore ONE deliberately ASYMMETRIC pirate reconstruction around the unchanged CENTERED native cockpit. Keep a short compact angular central core with full depth. The PORT side has a taller, longer solid armored engine cheek with a clipped trapezoidal top; the STARBOARD side has a lower shorter exposed engine seat and a deeply cut-back shoulder. Both rear-facing engines form an offset left/right pair, at slightly different fore-aft positions; both are visibly and solidly attached, never a loose jumble. The body should visibly differ from left to right in TOP but remain believable and balanced. Preserve three moving fan leaves PER SIDE with their compact forward roots and broadly similar flight span; brackets compensate for the unequal shoulders. Ornament survives as a fine stepped palmette field on the intact taller cheek, while the lower replaced side has a simpler broad angular fan and plain repair metal. Make the asymmetric volumes visible, not just different colors. Small centered roof hatch. No huge single off-center pod, no extra cabin, no round bulges. One of ten exploratory schemes, still clearly Liberty.
Label this sheet L40.
variants.visual_review: Асимметрия реализована геометрией: один борт выше и длиннее, двигатели смещены по высоте и продольной оси; различие видно на TOP и REAR. Это новая предлагаемая компоновка, а не исходная схема двигателя. Главный вид частично скрывает разнос бортов, поэтому TOP/REAR здесь важны. Веер трёхлистный, однако огибающая при складывании рядом с низким двигателем нуждается в проверке. Кабина остаётся исходной.

variants.architecture: narrow front / rising broad aft housing
variants.direction: The opposite mass distribution to a forward-shouldered ship: a slim low neck behind the original cabin grows into a strong HIGH, WIDE AFT WEDGE. Top edges diverge toward the stern; the side roof rises on two long crisp planar ramps, while the belly remains stepped. The aft section is a broad chamfered trapezoidal shell, with a deep central cutback accommodating TWO VERTICALLY STACKED unequal engine units on a narrow central seat. Those engine units remain visibly separate from the shell. A fixed broad diagonal tail face terminates the upper shell directly, no posts or spoiler bridge. Three slender clipped trapezoidal leaves per side are rooted far forward beneath the narrow waist and spread backward outside the widening hull; provide outboard stow clearance. Small roof hatch on the forward low shoulder, not occupying the rear ramp. Relief follows the rising planes in fan-shaped sloped fields and stepped borders that climb toward the stern. Broad rear mass, narrow front mass: no constant-width coffin and no cathedral silhouette.

variants.visual_review: Профиль явно нарастает от низкого носа к высокой корме; двигатели находятся внутри глубокой кормовой ниши, но читаются отдельными блоками. Сильный контраст с передней массой L35 и поперечной L38. Задняя оболочка получилась тяжёлой: это крайняя поисковая трактовка, а не автоматически принятая пропорция. Малые виды согласуют вертикальную пару. Проверка крыльев вокруг расширяющейся кормы остаётся задачей геометрии.

variants.architecture: narrow central upright wedge / low lateral propulsion
variants.direction: Use a narrow upright central HULL BLADE as the major fixed aft volume: a single solid sharply faceted trapezoidal ridge, rising modestly behind a low forward cockpit saddle and sloping back down at the stern. This is an integrated full-thickness hull/keel volume, not a thin decorative fin perched on a box, and not a tower; total height stays close to the source fighter's full height. Its deep side faces are shaped into diagonal inset bas-relief fields with a strong stylized fan and two stepped flute bands. The top-view core is deliberately NARROW. Two short LEFT/RIGHT engines sit LOW beside the rear base of this central wedge, clearly separated from it by deep designed notches and thick continuous root mounts. Wide three-leaf fan wings emerge from compact forward roots below the low saddle, one fan per side, and fold outside the engine seats. A small paired hatch occupies the forward saddle ahead of the raised wedge. The visual contrast is a narrow deep central mass with broad mobile fan planes and low propulsion, not a long high-sided rectangular block.

Три листа и компактный люк присутствуют; их кинематика и кабина требуют исходной геометрической привязки.

variants.visual_review: Два самостоятельных расширения корпуса соединены выраженной узкой талией: верхнее переднее плечо и более глубокий задний объём. Задняя часть может выглядеть тяжеловато — оставлена как отдельная попытка для выбора пользователя. Кинематика, глубина трюма и точное соответствие исходной кабине не проверены новым мешем.

user_direction: вот. с точки зрения стиля ты нащупал тему правильно. но с точки зрения реализции ваышло всё равно не то. постарайся отойти от идеи бруска с крыльями. и может вообще продумать другую схему. то есть поиграйся с формами. менять можно - в разумных пределах. но стиль "под ампир" должен остаться
batch_instruction: сделай 10 попыток. главное чтобы они были разные
design_change: Surface style of L33/L34 is positively received, architecture remains unaccepted. Explore ten genuinely different primary hull layouts, not ten frieze variations. Native cockpit unchanged. Wing fold principle and compact paired baydoor retained; moved roots/engines/door seats are proposed layouts requiring future geometry checks.

parameters.quality_steps: Built-in tool exposes no numeric step/quality setting.

scope: Offline concept art only. No ship chosen for modeling or deployment.
